title: Black musicians join Local 10 and win a lawsuit over the fee
summary: About 200 musicians asked to join Local 10, were charged $45 then $100, sued the International Musicians and won refunds.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, there was a break in that -- in the early '60s, before the integration. What was it, the CBS outlet here, -- Truck Parham...
Right, well, I was instrumental in that. This was a little after what we were talking about.

Before this was -- what happened was, a group of the musicians -- we went down to 10 before anything had happened, so far as mergers. It was -- the merger was only talk. So we went down and asked for permission to join 10, about 200 musicians.
Yes, this was after Petrillo was defeated.
Rudy Naschen, who was vice president, was the one who worked for this.

Yeah, right, see. So when we went down and we asked for this membership, the civil rights laws, whatever they were, wouldn't -- I mean, the lawyers, I guess, advised them that they couldn't very well afford to refuse us.

So they took us in, and then there was a big hassle about how much money to pay. So we paid $45 to join. And that was some kind of a figure between what the joiner fees were at 208 and what they were at 10. So then afterwards, -- pardon me -- they raised it to $100. And then we squawked on the $100, and had a lawyer, and we were the only ones to ever defeat the International Musicians, because we won the case. They had to refund these people their $100 back.
And then, all of the cost of the lawyers. So that's
